beats.say: Why do guys even have nipples?
Because they got them before they were guys.
beats.cap: BECAUSE THEY GOT THEM | *BEFORE* THEY WERE GUYS.

beats.say: Every embryo starts from the same basic blueprint.
beats.cap: EVERY EMBRYO STARTS | FROM THE *SAME* | BASIC BLUEPRINT.

beats.say: Nipples start forming around weeks four to six.
The gene that starts making an embryo male, called S R Y,
beats.cap: THE GENE THAT STARTS | MAKING AN EMBRYO *MALE,* | CALLED *SRY,*

beats.say: only switches on around week seven.
By then, the nipples are already there.
beats.cap: BY THEN, THE NIPPLES | ARE *ALREADY THERE.*

beats.say: So why didn't evolution delete them?
A popular explanation: they do no harm,
beats.cap: A POPULAR EXPLANATION: | THEY DO *NO HARM,*

beats.say: so there was no pressure to get rid of them.
beats.cap: SO THERE WAS | *NO PRESSURE* | TO GET RID OF THEM.

beats.say: Men can get breast cancer too. It's rare, but real.
beats.cap: MEN CAN GET | *BREAST CANCER* TOO. | IT'S RARE, BUT REAL.

beats.say: So see a doctor if a nipple or chest changes.
beats.cap: SO SEE A DOCTOR | IF A NIPPLE OR CHEST | *CHANGES.*

beats.say: So no, guys' nipples aren't a mistake.
beats.cap: SO NO, GUYS' NIPPLES | AREN'T A *MISTAKE.*

beats.say: They're a souvenir from week four.

sources.fact: UNSW Sydney (Michelle Moscova, via The Conversation), 'Why do men have nipples?': breasts and nipples start to form before the SRY gene has been activated, between weeks four and six; SRY is activated when the embryo is around seven weeks old; embryos of both sexes have primitive structures; some argue male nipples remain because they do no harm and there is no benefit in eliminating them; at birth boys' and girls' nipples and breasts look alike; men can develop breast cancer (0.5-1% of breast cancers) and nipple changes should be checked by a doctor

Discover Magazine, 'Why Do Men Have Nipples?': males and females start from the same genetic blueprint; nipples appear before sex differentiation; Stephen Jay Gould argued male nipples need no adaptive explanation because there is no selective pressure against a harmless trait

math.note: UNSW: nipples form weeks 4 to 6, before SRY activates around week 7
UNSW: SRY activated around seven weeks
UNSW: men are about 0.5 to 1% of breast cancers, so 'rare'

post.instagram_caption:
Why do guys have nipples? 🤔

Every embryo starts from the same basic blueprint. Nipples start forming around weeks 4 to 6, and the SRY gene that starts making an embryo male only switches on around week 7. By then the nipples are already there, and since they do no harm, there was no pressure for evolution to remove them.

Men can get breast cancer too, so see a doctor if a nipple or chest changes.

Sources: UNSW Sydney, Discover Magazine.
